title: voy a + verb, los, ver, verbs of movement

cards.title: Find the Latin equivalent
cards.body: When an English phrase like 'carry on' has no direct conversion, look for a Latin-origin word with the same meaning: continue → continuation → continuar.

cards.title: Don't test yourself — find it
cards.body: When a word doesn't come back, don't freeze on 'do I remember it or not?'. Ask what it was connected to (intento ↔ intention) and let it come back.

cards.title: demostrar, mostrar = to show
cards.body: Demostración has no n (demonstration → demostración). Remove de- from demostrar and you get mostrar, 'to show'.

cards.title: algo = something
cards.body: Combine it with te attached to the verb.

examples.en: I want to show you something.

cards.title: voy a + verb = I'm going to …
cards.body: As in English, 'I'm going to' talks about the future. Spanish adds a ('to') after voy because voy is a verb of movement, even when nobody is actually moving.

cards.title: los = them
cards.body: 'Them' is the plural of 'him', and Spanish shows it: lo + s = los.

cards.title: ver = to see — a only after movement
cards.body: Ver (think 'view') means to see. Only verbs of movement take the extra a: voy a verlos, but quiero verlos and intento verlos. Intentar is 'to try'.

examples.en: I'm going to try to see them.

cards.caveat: Not 'quiero a verlos': quiero isn't a verb of movement.

cards.title: pasar = to pass (by) — also takes a
cards.body: Pasar is another verb of movement, so it's followed by a. Lo can also mean formal 'you'.

examples.en: I'm going to pass by to visit you.
I'm going to try to pass by to visit you.
examples.es: Voy a intentar pasar a visitarte.

cards.title: Putting it together
cards.body: Quiero (no a) + pasar (movement, so a) + mostrarte algo.

examples.en: I want to pass by to show you something.

practice.en: I want to show you something.

practice.why: voy a + verb for the future.
No a after quiero; los = them.

practice.en: I'm going to try to see them.
practice.why: a after voy, but not after intentar.

practice.en: I'm going to pass by to visit you.
practice.why: pasar is movement too: pasar a visitarte.

practice.en: I want to pass by to show you something.
